sections.title: A-1: General Items
sections.summary: General preconstruction review checklist items: chain of command, roles/responsibilities, design/construction changes since bid, materials source certification, mix design submittals, CQC laboratory/personnel certifications, batch plant certification, construction schedule, subcontractor activities, haul roads/access points, and a joint half-day construction workshop.
sections.body: Appendix A provides a preconstruction review checklist for concrete pavement projects. The general items to review before construction begins are: identify the chain of command in the decision-making process; identify roles and responsibilities of key staff for all involved parties; review all design and construction changes issued since bid; obtain certification of materials sources; review mix design submittals; confirm CQC laboratory and personnel certifications; confirm batch plant certification and mixer efficiency tests; review the construction schedule; review subcontractor activities; review haul roads and access points; and conduct a joint half-day construction workshop with the project team.
key_points: Identify the chain of command in the decision-making process.
Identify roles and responsibilities of key staff for all involved parties.
Review all design and construction changes issued since bid.
Certify materials sources.
Review mix design submittals.
Confirm CQC laboratory and personnel certifications.
Confirm batch plant certification and mixer efficiency tests.
Review construction schedule and sub-contractor activities.
Review haul roads and access points.
Conduct a joint half-day construction workshop.
sections.applicability: Applies as the first, general-scope agenda item of the preconstruction review meeting for any concrete pavement project.

sections.title: A-2: Batching Activities
sections.summary: Preconstruction checklist items for concrete batching activities: stockpile management, and aggregate moistures and added mixture water.
sections.body: The preconstruction review of batching activities covers stockpile management practices and the control of aggregate moistures together with the added mixture water, to ensure the batched concrete mixture is consistent and matches the approved mix design.
key_points: Review stockpile management practices.
Review aggregate moistures and the resulting added mixture water.
sections.applicability: Applies to the preconstruction review of the batch plant's concrete batching activities.

sections.title: A-3: Subgrade
sections.summary: Preconstruction checklist items for subgrade preparation: soil testing reports, cut/fill plans, borrow/waste areas, acceptable fill, removal of organic/unacceptable soil, procedures for over-depth cuts, compaction requirements and acceptance testing, proof rolling requirements and acceptance criteria, and production rates/schedule.
sections.body: The preconstruction review of subgrade work covers: review of soil testing reports; cut and fill plans; borrow and waste areas; the definition of acceptable fill; removal of organic material or unacceptable soil; the procedure to follow when cut depths exceed the engineer's estimate; review of compaction requirements and acceptance testing (moisture and density); proof rolling requirements and acceptance criteria; and expected production rates and a tentative schedule for subgrade work.
key_points: Review soil testing reports.
Review cut and fill plans, and borrow and waste areas.
Define acceptable fill and procedures for removing organic or unacceptable soil.
Establish procedures for when cut depths exceed the engineer's estimate.
Review compaction requirements and acceptance testing (moisture and density).
Review proof rolling requirements and acceptance criteria.
Confirm expected production rates and tentative schedule.
sections.applicability: Applies to the preconstruction review of subgrade preparation, earthwork, and compaction acceptance for a concrete pavement project.

sections.title: A-4: Soil Stabilization (If Applicable)
sections.summary: Preconstruction checklist items for soil stabilization, applicable when the project includes stabilized subgrade: QC plan and soil data review, mix designs per soil type, field testing frequency, area division by stabilization requirements, field identification and approval responsibility, trimming and disposal, mixing/production requirements, lime spread rates, mixing passes, mellowing/curing periods, moisture control, temperature requirements, acceptance testing, and protection allowances for unprotected or re-trimmed stabilized soil.
sections.body: When soil stabilization is part of the project, the preconstruction review covers: review of the soil stabilization QC plan; review of soil data regarding stabilization requirements; mix design submittals for each soil type; field testing requirements and frequency (soil gradation, minus No. 200, plasticity, density, strength, lime/cement/fly ash content, depth, grade elevation); the tentative division of the project into areas based on soil stabilization requirements; how soil type and stabilization requirements will be identified in the field (visually or by plasticity testing); who in the field is responsible for approving soil stabilization requirements and acceptance; plasticity testing frequency or procedures used to further subdivide an area by soil type; trimming procedures and equipment, and disposal of trimmed material; initial mixing and production requirements, including calendar day restrictions; lime spread rates; minimum passes with mixing equipment; mellowing and curing periods; moisture control and limits during compaction; ambient temperature requirements prior to covering; acceptance testing frequency and procedures for moisture density, soil classification, pH, lime content, liquid and plastic limit, soluble sulfate, density, strength, and thickness; allowances for unprotected soil stabilization, including protection requirements for various time periods and paving seasons; allowances for finishing high and then re-trimming if stabilized soil is not protected; and expected production rates and a tentative schedule.
key_points: Review soil stabilization QC plan and soil data; confirm mix designs per soil type.
Set field testing requirements/frequency: gradation, minus No. 200, plasticity, density, strength, lime/cement/fly ash content, depth, grade elevation.
Divide the project into areas based on stabilization requirements; define field identification method and approval responsibility.
Establish trimming procedures/equipment and disposal of trimmed material.
Set mixing/production requirements (calendar day restrictions), lime spread rates, minimum mixing passes, mellowing/curing periods.
Control moisture during compaction and set ambient temperature requirements prior to covering.
Define acceptance testing frequency for moisture density, classification, pH, lime content, Atterberg limits, soluble sulfate, density, strength, thickness.
Define protection allowances for unprotected stabilized soil and for finishing high then re-trimming.
Confirm expected production rates and tentative schedule.
sections.applicability: Applies to the preconstruction review of soil stabilization work when the project includes a stabilized subgrade.

sections.title: A-5: Stabilized Base
sections.summary: Preconstruction checklist items for stabilized base: QC plan, mix design submittal, specifications/lot areas, mixing/quantity verification, water content/strength/thickness/grade testing and acceptance, weather limitations and nonconformance procedures, placement and cold joints, rough grading/finish rolling, jointing, curing requirements, aggregate durability/soundness/abrasion/gradation data, and grade survey decision authority.
sections.body: The preconstruction review of stabilized base covers: review of base stabilization in the QC plan; mix design submittal; specifications and lot areas; mixing procedures and quantity verification; water content, strength, thickness verification, and grade testing and acceptance procedures; weather (temperature) limitations for mixing and placement and nonconformance procedures for under-thick, under-strength, and over-strength material; placement procedures and cold joints; rough grading and finish rolling procedures; jointing procedures; moist curing and curing membrane requirements (coverage, time, and material); aggregate durability, soundness, abrasion, and gradation test data and requirements; and grade survey issues, including who decides what action to take if grade is a concern.
key_points: Review base stabilization QC plan and mix design submittal, plus specifications and lot areas.
Verify mixing procedures and quantity; verify water content, strength, thickness, and grade testing/acceptance.
Set weather (temperature) limitations and nonconformance procedures for under-thick, under-strength, over-strength material.
Review placement procedures, cold joints, rough grading, and finish rolling procedures.
Review jointing procedures and moist curing/curing membrane requirements (coverage, time, material).
Confirm aggregate durability, soundness, abrasion, and gradation test data/requirements.
Establish grade survey decision authority for grade concerns.
sections.applicability: Applies to the preconstruction review of a stabilized (treated) base course beneath the concrete pavement.

sections.title: A-6: Concrete Paving/Placing/Finishing/Texturing/Curing
sections.summary: Preconstruction checklist items for the concrete paving operation: placement/filler lane scheduling, base conditioning, equipment breakdown procedures, maximum haul times, placement procedures, thickness verification, hot/cold weather precautions, vibrator testing/consolidation, curing/texturing, dowel drill-and-epoxy grouting, tie bar/dowel alignment verification, straight edge/edge slump tolerances, and treatment of the four early distress types (plastic shrinkage cracking, edge slump, joint spalling, full-depth cracking).
sections.body: The preconstruction review of concrete paving, placing, finishing, texturing, and curing covers: placement and filler lane scheduling; base conditioning; equipment breakdown procedures; maximum concrete haul times; placement procedures; thickness verification during placement; hot/cold weather specifications and precautions; vibrator testing and consolidation issues; curing and texturing procedures; drill and epoxy grouting of dowel bars; tie bar/dowel alignment, spacing, and offset verification; straight edge and edge slump tolerances; and the treatment of plastic shrinkage cracking, edge slump, joint spalling, and full-depth cracking (as detailed in Chapter 11, Early Distress Repair).
key_points: Review placement and filler lane scheduling, base conditioning, and equipment breakdown procedures.
Confirm maximum concrete haul times and placement procedures; verify thickness during placement.
Establish hot/cold weather specifications and precautions.
Review vibrator testing/consolidation issues and curing/texturing procedures.
Confirm drill-and-epoxy grouting of dowel bars, and tie bar/dowel alignment, spacing, and offset verification.
Set straight edge and edge slump tolerances.
Confirm treatments for plastic shrinkage cracking, edge slump, joint spalling, and full-depth cracking.
sections.applicability: Applies to the preconstruction review of the concrete paving, placing, finishing, texturing, and curing operations.

sections.title: A-7: Joint Sawcutting
sections.summary: Preconstruction checklist items for joint sawcutting: QC plan review, early-entrant saw use, backup saws, rain/skip-sawing procedures, reservoir/sealing installation and acceptance, sawcutting sequence and acceptable raveling, cut dimension tolerances, sealant/backer rod submittals, residue removal, joint beveling, curing time, cleanliness/moisture requirements before sealing, sealant depth tolerances, priming, equipment, ambient temperature limits, and inspection procedures.
sections.body: The preconstruction review of joint sawcutting covers: review of the sawcutting QC plan; use of early entrant saws; backup saws; rain conditions and skip sawing procedures; reservoir and sealing installation and acceptance procedures; sawcutting sequence and acceptable degree of sawcut raveling; initial and reservoir cut dimension tolerances and dimensions; joint sealant and backer rod material submittals; removal and flushing of joint sawing residue; joint beveling procedures; sealant and concrete curing time; sand blasting, reservoir cleanliness, and moisture condition requirements before sealing; sealant depth tolerances; reservoir priming material requirements; sealant pump, water truck, and sawcutting equipment; allowable ambient temperatures during sealing operations and compression seal reservoir requirements; and joint inspection procedures.
key_points: Review the sawcutting QC plan, early-entrant saw use, and backup saws.
Establish rain conditions and skip sawing procedures.
Review reservoir and sealing installation/acceptance procedures, sawcutting sequence, and acceptable raveling.
Set initial and reservoir cut dimension tolerances; confirm sealant and backer rod material submittals.
Confirm residue removal/flushing, joint beveling, and sealant/concrete curing time.
Set sand blasting, reservoir cleanliness, moisture, and sealant depth requirements before sealing.
Confirm reservoir priming material and sealing equipment (pump, water truck, sawcutting equipment).
Set allowable ambient temperatures during sealing and compression seal reservoir requirements.
Establish joint inspection procedures.
sections.applicability: Applies to the preconstruction review of the joint sawcutting and joint sealing operations for a concrete pavement project.

sections.title: A-8: CQC Activities
sections.summary: Preconstruction checklist items for Contractor Quality Control activities: QC plan review, aggregate durability/soundness/abrasion/gradation data, reinforcing steel/dowel bar submittals, sampling/testing procedures, control charts, mix design/w-cm ratio effects, beam sampling and testing, pay factor computation, thickness test locations, partial lots, treatment of premature cracking/spalling, edge slump/smoothness testing, nonconformance actions, documentation, and referee testing.
sections.body: The preconstruction review of CQC activities covers: review of the contractor's QC plan; aggregate durability, soundness, abrasion, and gradation test data and requirements; reinforcing steel and dowel bar submittals; materials sampling and testing procedures; use of control charts; concrete mixture designs and w/cm ratio effects on strength; concrete beam sampling, fabrication, curing, and testing procedures; sampling and pay factor computation overview; effects of strength/thickness variability on pay factor; determining locations for thickness tests; partial lots consideration; treatment of premature cracking and spalling; edge slump and smoothness testing and timing; actions to be taken if specification requirements are not met; documentation of test results and deviations; and verification of failing acceptance tests, retesting, and referee testing.
key_points: Review the contractor's QC plan and aggregate durability/soundness/abrasion/gradation test data.
Confirm reinforcing steel and dowel bar submittals, and materials sampling/testing procedures.
Use control charts; review mix designs and w/cm ratio effects on strength.
Confirm concrete beam sampling, fabrication, curing, and testing procedures.
Review sampling and pay factor computation, and effects of strength/thickness variability on pay factor.
Determine thickness test locations and partial lots consideration.
Confirm treatment of premature cracking/spalling and edge slump/smoothness testing and timing.
Define actions if specification requirements are not met; document test results and deviations.
Establish verification of failing acceptance tests, retesting, and referee testing.
sections.applicability: Applies to the preconstruction review of Contractor Quality Control (CQC) plans, testing, and pay factor procedures for a concrete pavement project.
